_about: intake ② 개념 정의 — 목표(S1 · S2 · S3)가 무엇을 가리키는지 R1(상태 분석) 논문의 원문 문장으로 적는다. 단서표(intake_cues.json)는 팀 요약이고 이것은 원문 그대로다 — 줄바꿈 · 하이픈 · 쪽 넘김만 정리했고, 스캔본 N01은 텍스트 층의 OCR 오류를 쪽 이미지로 바로잡았다. page는 PDF 쪽 번호. ③ 목표 추론 입력에 통째로 넣고, 추론한 목표(와 부목표)의 정의를 IntakeResult.goal_evidence로 Reference 카드에 싣는다. 문장이 열 개 남짓이라 검색(RAG)하지 않는다.

S1.sentence: Repetitive negative thinking (RNT) poses such a transdiagnostic process being defined as a thinking process that is repetitive, passive, and/or relatively uncontrollable, and focused on negative content (Ehring & Watkins, 2008).
Rumination is a common form of repetitive negative thinking involving persistent distressing thoughts (Martin & Tesser, 2006; Nolen-Hoeksema et al., 2008).

Rumination has recently been conceptualized as a state-dependent cognitive response, triggered by situational factors such as perceived discrepancies between goals and current circumstances (Michel-Kröhler et al., 2023; Smith & Alloy, 2009; Tamm et al., 2024).

S2.sentence: Stress means a situation in which a person feels tense, restless, nervous or anxious or is unable to sleep at night because his/her mind is troubled all the time.
The first questionnaire measures state anxiety (how one feels at the moment), the second, trait anxiety (how one generally feels).

The evidence suggests that these interrelationships can be represented by a spatial model in which affective concepts fall in a circle in the following order: pleasure (0°), excitement (45°), arousal (90°), distress (135°), displeasure (180°), depression (225°), sleepiness (270°), and relaxation (315°).

S3.sentence: More formally, any prolonged mental effort leads to directed attention fatigue.
Any time one has worked intensely on a project and subsequently finds oneself mentally exhausted, one has experienced this unwelcome state.

Mental fatigue represents a psychobiological state with subjective (e.g., an increase in feelings of tiredness), behavioral (e.g., motivation decrease or reaction time increase), and physiological (e.g., alterations in the electroencephalogram signal) derivations in humans [6].

This psychobiological state is caused by brain-demanding tasks (i.e., mental load), with a relevant role of emotional (e.g., anxiety or stress) and cognitive (e.g., working memory or cognitive flexibility) aspects [6].
